newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia hosts E.Europe airspace conference.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia hosts E.Europe airspace conference.

text.p: A three-day conference on Central European Regional Airspace Management, hosted by Slovenia's Defence Ministry together with the U.S. Air Force, starts on Tuesday in the northwestern city of Bled.

The conference, grouping 22 central and eastern European nations, will focus on the Baltic states of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia with the U.S. Air Force advising on airspace management and air sovereignty in those countries.
The conference is aimed at promoting airspace management planning initiatives to help former communist countries modernise and integrate their systems with Western Europe, organisers said.

After the break-up of the pre-1990 military and political alignment, central and eastern European countries were left with antiquated air traffic control systems, poorly equipped air forces and with the military in charge of the use and control of airspace.

The U.S. Air Force's Electronic Systems Center (ESC) has also invited Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Albania, Romania, Slovenia, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Macedonia, Austria, Switzerland, Belarus, Croatia and Russia to participate in the meeting.
The ESC is the department in charge of command, control, communication, computer and intelligence systems in the Air Force.
"This conference is certainly a significant step towards integration of military and civil air-traffic control systems in these countries," ESC spokesman Jack Rankin told Reuters.
This year the U.S. offered $10 million for the modernisation of national command centres in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia.
The United States has promised to increase the amount to $25 million by the end of 1997.
Slovenian Defence Minister Jelko Kacin said the conference would give the host nation a chance to show off the great strides it has taken in terms of airspace management.

"The conference will show that Slovenia is several steps ahead of the central and eastern European states in terms of air-traffic control technology and its compatibility with NATO's technology," Kacin told a news conference.
